events.title: Gore by 5,708
events.text: Al Gore carried Wisconsin by 5,708 votes, two-tenths of a point.

events.title: Doyle elected
events.text: Jim Doyle, a Democrat, beat Governor Scott McCallum.

events.title: Kerry by 11,384
events.text: John Kerry carried Wisconsin by 11,384 votes.

events.title: Obama by 14
events.text: Barack Obama carried Wisconsin by almost fourteen points.

events.title: Walker elected
events.text: Scott Walker, the Milwaukee County Executive, was elected governor.

events.title: Tiffany to Assembly
events.text: Tom Tiffany, a former tour-boat operator and dam tender, won a seat in the Assembly.

events.title: Act 10
events.text: Act 10 removed most collective-bargaining rights for most public employees; protesters filled the Capitol.

events.title: Walker survives recall
events.text: On 5 June Walker won a recall election by almost seven points, the first U.S. governor to survive one.

events.title: Mining law
events.text: On 11 March Walker signed an iron-mining law written by Tiffany, now a state senator, in Rhinelander.

events.title: Trump by 22,748
events.text: Donald Trump carried Wisconsin by 22,748 votes, the first Republican to win it since 1984.

events.title: Crowley elected
events.text: David Crowley, a community organiser, won a seat in the Assembly from Milwaukee's north side.

events.title: Evers beats Walker
events.text: Tony Evers, the state schools superintendent, beat Walker by 29,227 votes.

events.title: Baldwin re-elected
events.text: On the same ballot Senator Tammy Baldwin, a Democrat, won by almost eleven points.

events.title: County executive
events.text: On 7 April Crowley was elected Milwaukee County Executive by 1,026 votes, the first Black person elected to the post.

events.title: Tiffany to Congress
events.text: On 12 May Tiffany won a special election for the U.S. House in northern Wisconsin's 7th District.

events.title: Biden by 20,682
events.text: Joe Biden carried Wisconsin by 20,682 votes.

events.title: Electoral objections
events.text: On 6 and 7 January Tiffany voted for objections to Arizona's and Pennsylvania's electoral votes; both failed.

events.title: Evers re-elected
events.text: Evers won by 90,239 votes, while Republican Ron Johnson won the Senate race on the same ballot.

events.title: Court flips
events.text: Janet Protasiewicz won a Supreme Court seat by eleven points, giving liberals a majority.

events.title: Act 12
events.text: A bipartisan law raised state aid to local governments and let Milwaukee County raise its sales tax to pay pension debt.

events.title: New maps
events.text: On 19 February Evers signed new legislative maps after the Supreme Court struck down the old ones.

events.title: Trump by 29,397
events.text: Donald Trump carried Wisconsin by 29,397 votes.

events.title: Split ticket
events.text: On the same ballot Baldwin won re-election by 28,781 votes.

events.title: Record court race
events.text: Susan Crawford won a Supreme Court race by about ten points; spending neared $115 million.

events.title: 1849 law struck down
events.text: On 2 July the Supreme Court ruled, 4 to 3, that an 1849 abortion ban was no longer in force.

events.title: Evers steps aside
events.text: On 24 July Governor Evers said he would not seek a third term.

events.title: Crowley runs
events.text: On 9 September Crowley launched his campaign with a video about his family's evictions.

events.title: Tiffany runs
events.text: On 23 September Tiffany entered the race; his first rally was in Wausau.

events.title: Port Washington
events.text: A data-centre campus of more than $15 billion was announced in Port Washington.

events.title: Beaver Dam
events.text: Meta announced a data centre of more than $1 billion in Beaver Dam.

events.title: Trump endorses Tiffany
events.text: On 27 January President Trump endorsed Tiffany; Josh Schoemann left the race the next day.

events.title: Court majority grows
events.text: On 7 April Chris Taylor won a Supreme Court seat by twenty points; liberals now hold five of seven seats.

events.title: Out, then back in
events.text: Crowley left the race on 8 July and re-entered on 18 July with Evers's endorsement.

events.title: Act 10 upheld
events.text: On 29 July a state appeals court upheld Act 10, 2 to 1.

events.title: Under 5,000 dairy farms
events.text: On 1 August Wisconsin's licensed dairy herds fell below 5,000 for the first time; in 1930 there were about 167,000.

events.title: Primary night
events.text: On 11 August Crowley beat Francesca Hong by 3,673 votes; Tiffany won 95 percent.

events.title: Lake Wausau landing
events.text: On 12 September Tiffany's small plane lost power and landed in Lake Wausau; he and the pilot swam to safety.

events.title: Marquette poll
events.text: In late September the Marquette Law School Poll found Crowley 49, Tiffany 46 among likely voters.

events.title: One debate
events.text: The candidates agreed to one televised debate, on 21 October in Milwaukee.

events.title: Election Day
events.text: On 3 November Wisconsin chooses between Crowley and Tiffany.

eras: The closest state: Gore, Kerry, Obama
chartNote: Each state is coloured by the margin of the most recent presidential popular vote (Democratic minus Republican share of all votes; certified state results). It is a simplification: Wisconsin chooses its governor in its own race, and Wisconsinites split their tickets (in 2024 Donald Trump carried the state while a Democrat won its Senate seat), so the presidential colour is a backdrop, not a forecast. Shares are of land area, not of people or votes: about a quarter of Wisconsin's votes are cast in Milwaukee and Dane counties. Boundaries are today's states (Natural Earth); the map is framed on Wisconsin, so outer states are cut at the edge.
